messages.content: How do I save a website as a favorite in Edge on my computer?

Here is how to save the page you are on as a favorite in Microsoft Edge:

1. Open Microsoft Edge and go to the website.
2. Select the **Add this page to favorites** button in the address bar.
3. If you like, type a new name or choose a different folder.
4. Select **Done**.

If you do not see that button in the address bar, select **Settings and more**, then **Favorites**, then **More options**, then **Add this page to favorites**.

Yes. You can do it from the menu, since the crossword page is already open:

3. Select **More options**.
4. Select **Add this page to favorites**.

That saves only the page you are on.

My husband mentioned there is a way to do it from the keyboard without going into any menus, and I would rather learn that. I have a mouse with a wheel on it too if that helps.

Yes, there are two quick ways. With the news page open:

2. Roll the mouse wheel up to make the page bigger. Roll it down to make it smaller.

messages.content: A website keeps letting pop-ups through in Chrome on my computer. How do I block pop-ups for that site? I can see it in the allowed list.

messages.content: How do I make Chrome my default browser on my Windows 11 computer?

Here is how to do it on Windows 11:

1. Click **Start**.
2. Open **Settings**.
3. Click **Apps**, then **Default apps**.
4. Under **Set defaults for applications**, type **Chrome** in the search box.
5. Select **Google Chrome**.
6. At the top, click **Set default** next to **Make Google Chrome your default browser**.
7. Review the list under **Set default file types or link types** and check that Chrome is chosen for the types you need.

messages.content: How do I have Chrome save my password on my computer, and how do I look at it later?

Here is how to save a password in Chrome:

1. Go to the website's sign-in page.
2. Type your username and password, then submit the form.
3. When Chrome asks to save the password, select **Save**.

To find it later:
1. At the top right, click **More**.
2. Click **Passwords and autofill**, then **Google Password Manager**.
3. Under **Passwords**, select the password.
4. On the right of your password, select **Show password**.

sources.title: Chrome Help: Manage passwords in Chrome

messages.content: I keep all my website passwords written in a little notebook next to my computer and my son says Chrome can hold them for me instead. I use Chrome on my Windows computer. Chrome has never offered to save any of them. Can I type one in myself so Chrome has it, without waiting for it to ask me?

Yes, you can add a password yourself:

1. At the top right, click **More**.
2. Click **Passwords and autofill**, then **Google Password Manager**.
3. Select **Add**.
4. Enter the website, your username, and your password.
5. Select **Save**.

Repeat these steps for each password in your notebook.

messages.content: My husband and I share one Windows computer and Chrome has my passwords saved. I don't want him to be able to just click and see them. Can I make Chrome check that it is really me before it shows a saved password?

Yes. On Windows, you can turn on a check:

1. At the top right, click **More**.
2. Click **Passwords and autofill**, then **Google Password Manager**.
3. Select **Settings**.
4. Turn on **Use Windows Hello when filling passwords**.
5. Follow the on-screen instructions to confirm.

Once it is on, Windows Hello is used when Chrome fills in a saved password, and this check can also cover revealing, copying, or editing a password. The setting is optional and off by default, so it stays off until you turn it on.
